correctness.rationale: Exact local-residue count gives factor 1-4/Q+2/Q² for short primes away from the shift, 1-2/Q² for long primes away from shift, and 1-(1+1[v_P(a)=1])/Q² for primes dividing shift. CRT exact equidistribution for monics once degree exceeds modulus degree, with a uniform bound 2 sum_{d>K} pi_2(d)2^{-2d}, rigorously establishes the infinite product. The only negative local factors are norm-two primes, so sign is parity of the number of roots of a in F_2. Polynomial irreducible-counting gives -log F_M=H_M+o(1), proving M^4 L_a(M) converges to the specified nonzero constant by an absolutely convergent normalized Euler product. An independent stdlib verifier passed 100 exhaustive mod-P² local factor tests and explicit monic enumerations; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The motivating two-point truncated-Möbius analysis excludes the singular norm-two case. The new result resolves that natural missing base field, proves every fixed-cutoff correlation is nonzero and can be negative, gives an exact root-parity sign classification for all nonzero shifts, and determines a sharp quartic cutoff law with explicit signed Euler-product constant. These structural phenomena explain why norm-two local factors require special treatment; this is not a finite table or arbitrary invariant. The order of limits is explicitly restricted.
